activity.notes: Emperor Zhenzong (Zhao Heng) ruled the Northern Song from 997 to 1022. His reign belongs to the dynasty's founding-and-consolidation phase; the 1005 Chanyuan Covenant with the Liao ended decades of Song-Liao warfare and inaugurated a long-lived frontier settlement.

sources.title: Founding and Consolidation of the Sung Dynasty under T’ai-tsu (960–976), T’ai-tsung (976–997), and Chen-tsung (997–1022)
sources.citation_text: Lau Nap-yin and Huang K’uan-chung, in The Cambridge History of China, identify Chen-tsung (Emperor Zhenzong) as reigning from 997 to 1022 and treat his reign as part of the Song dynasty's founding and consolidation.

sources.title: The Fragility of Peace: Song China's Northwestern Frontier and Erosion of the Chanyuan Paradigm in the Mid-Eleventh Century
sources.citation_text: Paul Jakov Smith describes the 1005 Chanyuan Covenant between Song Zhenzong and Liao Shengzong as ending twenty-five years of war and establishing a durable political model for Song frontier policy.
